hook.text: When Disney bought Pixar for $7.4 billion, both sides needed the deal—but who needed it more?

buildup.text: M&A negotiations involve valuation battles: buyers want to pay less, sellers want to sell for more.

discovery.text: Due diligence reveals hidden information. Knowing the target's true value shifts bargaining power.

twist.text: Bidding wars destroy buyer value. When multiple suitors compete, the winner often overpays—the winner's curse.

climax.text: The 'poison pill' defense changes the game: it makes acquisition so expensive that hostile bids become unviable.

punchline.text: The buyer who wants it most pays the most.

quiz.question: What is the winner's curse in acquisitions?
options: The winning bidder tends to overpay
